note: FuzzedDataProvider consumes a variable-length string from the raw input bytes; this string becomes the UTF-8 input to the transcoder.
The crafted input is valid UTF-8, so the code proceeds to the UTF-32 conversion path.
Buffer size is allocated based on the actual number of code points in the input; for the crafted input this is N code points.
Heap buffer of exactly N char32_t elements is allocated; any write beyond N elements is a heap-buffer-overflow.
Calls the westmere implementation's convert_utf8_to_utf32 which processes the input in 64-byte SIMD blocks.
The safety_margin counts only 4 leading bytes from the end; this is insufficient to prevent overflows from the SIMD kernel which can write up to 16 code points per 16-byte chunk.
The SIMD loop processes 64-byte blocks; the crafted input is long enough that the SIMD path is taken for the vulnerable block.
The mask is computed from the leading-byte positions; for the crafted pattern of alternating 1-byte and 4-byte code units, the mask maps to an index in the 145-208 range.

code: size_t consumed = convert_masked_utf8_to_utf32(in + pos, utf8_end_of_code_point_mask, utf32_output);
note: Calls the vulnerable convert_masked_utf8_to_utf32 function which can write more code points than the actual number of code units in the input.
The mask maps to an index in the 145-208 range, which corresponds to 2 input code units but the code writes 3 code points.
Loads the shuffle pattern for the 2-code-unit case; the pattern extracts bytes for 2 code units (e.g., 1-byte + 4-byte).
Shuffles the input bytes according to the pattern; for a 1-byte + 4-byte pair, this produces 2 code points worth of data.
Composes the UTF-32 code points; the shuffle pattern produces 3 code point slots even though only 2 code units exist.
Writes 3 char32_t values (12 bytes) to the output buffer, but only 2 code points should be written for 2 code units; this is a 1-code-point overflow.
Advances the output pointer by 3 code points, but only 2 code units were consumed; repeated occurrences in the 64-byte block accumulate the overflow.
With 4 such 1-byte+4-byte pairs in the 64-byte block, the total overflow is 4 code points (16 bytes), causing a heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of 16 bytes past the allocated buffer.
